name: Sudoku Mathematical Integrity & Unique Solver Engine
greenMarker: Sudoku Mathematical Integrity, Immutability & Solver Engine 100% Verified

mutations.name: the generator export is renamed
mutations.why: An import-contract check, not a behaviour one. It was called "the generator stops guaranteeing a unique solution", but renaming an export makes the gate die at load — it would fail identically if the generator were perfect, so it proved nothing about uniqueness. Kept under an honest name, because a renamed export is a real way to break the suite, and paired with the behaviour mutation below that actually removes the guarantee.

mutations.name: the generator stops restoring a clue whose removal creates a second solution
mutations.why: The guarantee itself, removed. generatePuzzle blanks cells at random and puts one back whenever countSolutions says the board now has more than one answer; skipping that restore ships puzzles with several valid answers. The gate used to accept this — it asserted the puzzle was solvable and that the solver s answer matched the solution shipped beside it, which stays true of an ambiguous board, and the word unique appeared only in its heading. It now counts solutions with a brute force that shares no code with the engine, because using the engine s own countSolutions would let the generator mark its own work.
